stories.headline: Harsh winter looms over LoC villages
stories.title: Harsh winter looms over LoC villages
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 23: As Kashmir prepares for another harsh winter, residents living along the Line of Control (LoC) in north Kashmir’s Uri, Kupwara and other border areas are bracing for months of biting cold, difficult road conditions and uncertainty over access to essential services. For families living in villages close to the LoC, winter is not merely a change in weather. It brings the challenge of keeping homes warm, arranging firewood and other heating materials, reaching hospitals during emergencies and protecting children and elderly family members when snowfall cuts off roads and temperatures plunge. In several border villages, where settlements are scattered across steep slopes and remote mountain terrain, the onset of winter also raises concerns over the availability of safe shelters, reliable electricity, drinking water and the continuation of livelihoods that sustain families through the year. From Uri in Baramulla district to the border belts of Kupwara, residents say that while improved connectivity and relief measures have helped in recent years, the hardships associated with living close to the LoC continue to shape their daily lives. “Winter is always a difficult time for us. We have to arrange firewood, food supplies and other essentials well before the snowfall begins. Once the roads become slippery or get blocked, even a short journey can become a major challenge,” said Lal Hussain Kohli, a resident of Charunda village in Uri. Residents said that families with young children, elderly members and patients requiring regular medical attention are particularly vulnerable during prolonged spells of snowfall. In Uri, which has several villages close to the LoC, winter preparedness begins well before the first major snowfall. Residents in areas such as Charunda, Garkote, Nambla, Kamalkote and other border settlements have to prepare for the possibility of disrupted transport and restricted movement. The memories of past periods of cross-border shelling remain fresh for many families, particularly those whose houses were damaged or who had to seek shelter during firing. For residents, bunkers are an important part of winter and emergency preparedness. However, the availability, condition and accessibility of these structures remain significant concerns, especially for families living in vulnerable locations. “During shelling, a bunker can mean the difference between safety and danger. But the real question is whether every vulnerable household has access to a safe and usable shelter. Some families have to move considerable distances to reach a protected place,” said Tariq Hashim, a local of Kamalkote village of Uri. Residents have also raised concerns about the maintenance of existing bunkers, drainage, ventilation and their suitability for elderly people and children. In villages where bunkers are located away from homes, reaching them during darkness, heavy rain or snow can become difficult. Residents said that road maintenance, timely snow clearance and reliable emergency transport should be prioritised in villages where alternative routes are limited. In Kupwara district, particularly in the Karnah, Keran, Machil and other remote border belts, difficult terrain and heavy snowfall can compound the problems associated with living near the LoC. In areas where roads pass through mountainous stretches, snowfall and icy conditions can slow traffic or temporarily disrupt movement. For residents, this can affect access to healthcare, educational institutions, markets and government offices. “Before winter, we try to stock essential supplies because nobody knows how long difficult weather will last. If the road is blocked and someone falls ill, the family faces enormous stress. Reaching a hospital in time becomes the biggest concern,” said Tahir Ahmad, a resident of a remote Kupwara border village. Hilal Ahmad, another local from the district said challenges are particularly acute for pregnant women, elderly people and patients suffering from conditions that require regular treatment. Alongside government departments and local administrations, the Army plays an important role in supporting communities living in remote border areas, particularly during emergencies and difficult weather conditions. As winter approaches, residents are seeking practical measures to reduce the hardships they face every year.

stories.headline: PLA’s patrolling behaviour keeps LAC disturbed, Govt. says
stories.title: PLA’s patrolling behaviour keeps LAC disturbed, Govt. says
stories.summary: MEA says “Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns”; video of ITBP chief’s remarks on situation in Arunachal Pradesh removed after The Hindu’s report on the border situation; Congress slams government for suppressing information
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Line of Actual Control (LAC) has been “disturbed” by the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) patrolling behaviour, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday (October 23, 2026) in response to questions about a report in The Hindu on skirmishes along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh.
The report, which had quoted the outgoing Director General of the Indo-Tibetan Border.
Police Forces (ITBP), Shatrujeet Kapur, expressing concern over “face-offs” underway since July 2026, drew sharp criticism from the Congress.
Despite the Ministry’s confirmation, the video of Mr. Kapur’s speech, given at an event in Alwar on Thursday (October 22, 2026), was deleted from the ITBP’s official YouTube channel.

This was the first time the government has officially accepted that, more than two years after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping announced a détente between their militaries, the border areas remain tense and “get disturbed” over patrolling routes.

“As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told journalists at a briefing here, blaming the PLA for the divergences.

“Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control,” he added, directing queries on the specific situation to the Ministry of Defence.

Mr. Jaiswal also reiterated the government’s position since the beginning of the four-year military standoff at the LAC, including the Galwan clashes in 2020, that the “maintenance of peace and tranquility in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations”, and said that both sides were in touch about improving their understanding of the LAC for “better border management”.
In a post on X, Mr. Kharge said the confirmation by the chief of ITBP forces stationed at the LAC was “deeply alarming”.
The Congress chief alleged that Mr. Modi’s June 2020 statement that no one had entered Indian territory after the Galwan clashes had emboldened China.

Addressing a press conference, Congress media and publicity department chairman, Pawan Khera, commended the ITBP’s ‘Shaurya Commandos’ for handling the confrontations with China, but accused the government of suppressing information from the border.

“The fact that China has entered our territory does not bother [the government]; what bothers them is that this has been reported,” Mr. Khera said, adding that “image is more important for them than the country’s interests”.

stories.headline: A new era of leadership: Visionaries, innovators and changemakers
stories.title: A new era of leadership: Visionaries, innovators and changemakers
stories.summary: The future is shaped by individuals who look beyond established boundaries, challenge conventional thinking and turn their knowledge into meaningful action. Across industries, leadership is taking new forms, driven by innovation, specialised expertise, personal conviction and a growing focus on creating lasting value.From entrepreneurship, healthcare and taxation to education, art, mental wellness, spirituality and child rights, today's changemakers are contributing to conversations that extend beyond their immediate professions. Through their work, they are addressing evolving needs, empowering individuals, sharing knowledge and exploring new ways to create a positive impact.What connects these diverse journeys is a commitment to growth and the belief that meaningful progress begins with a clear purpose. Whether through professional excellence, creative expression, personal transformation or social responsibility, each individual brings a distinct perspective to the challenges and opportunities of the present.As industries and communities continue to evolve, their stories offer a closer look at how experience, innovation and determination can translate into action. Together, these visionaries reflect a broader understanding of success, one that values not only individual achievements but also the ideas, contributions and possibilities they bring to the world around them.Ms. Preetty G. SharmaPreetty G. Sharma, Founder of astro divine energy, is an Astrologer and spiritual guidance practitioner with over 25 years of experience, working with individuals / corporations across 30+ countries. Her approach combines astrology-based insights, spiritual practices and Divine Power to help people navigate challenges related to relationships, family, career, business, finances and personal growth. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she states that her guidance and work with Divine Power helped save lots of lives and support families through circumstances. Her mission is to connect one person in every family with Divine Power, encouraging self-awareness, lasting change, kindness and conscious living. Through her work, Preetty seeks to guide people towards a better future and success in life .Dr. Rajni RathiDr. Rajni Rathi is a Vastu and Astrology expert with over 20 years of experience in guiding individuals and organisations towards balance, harmony and purposeful growth. Her expertise combines traditional wisdom with contemporary perspectives on energy alignment, spatial harmony and the five elements. She has guided thousands of individuals and organisations, helping them understand the role of spaces, energy and balance in personal and professional environments. Recognised for her contributions to the field, she has received several national and international honours, including the Lifetime Achievement Award. She is also the owner of Würfel on MG Road, Delhi, a premium modular kitchen and wardrobe brand inspired by European design and craftsmanship.Vinod Kumar GinjalaVinod Kumar Ginjala, Founder and Managing Director of Gravita Oasis Review Solutions Pvt Ltd, focuses on strengthening U.S. home health operations through medical coding, clinical documentation review, quality assurance and technology. A Bachelor of Pharmacy graduate, he holds the Certified Professional Coder (CPC), COQS and BCHH-C certifications. He founded Gravita in 2021, drawing on his healthcare and home health coding experience. His work addresses documentation inconsistencies, strengthens review processes and supports accurate coding decisions. He is also working on AI-driven solutions for the home health sector, with a focus on making documentation and coding workflows more efficient and reliable. His vision is to combine healthcare expertise, technology and education to build practical solutions for evolving home health needs.CA Jayesh GogriCA Jayesh Gogri has specialised in indirect taxation for nearly three decades. In 2012, he co-founded GSC Intime Services, where he is Director, advising business houses on GST, customs and government incentives, now across 40+ cities in India. His firm's mantra is simple: "Solve the issue!" He and GSC received the ET Business Excellence Award 2026 from The Times Group, and he shared the BCAS Jal Erach Dastur Award for Best Feature (2025-26). He has delivered 200+ talks at forums including IIM and ICAI, and authored books including GST Margdarshika in four languages. Guided by value before fees, he is now writing a book on living joyfully despite all odds.Josephine M DiasJosephine M Dias spent 29+ years as an educator at St Thomas' Girls School, Delhi, before reinventing herself after retirement. After competing at 59, she became VG Mrs India Empress 2nd Runner-Up 2025 and joined VG Pageants as a team member, guiding women from different backgrounds through their pageant journeys. A certified health coach shaped by her own transformation journey, she wrote OMG! Don't Try Adventure With Your Health, which champions Medicine 3.0 and prevention before cure. She also holds the Magnetic Personality Award in public speaking from Sneh Desai and works with AstoneaOne. Her message: listen to your body when it whispers, it shouldn't have to scream to get your attention.RiyaaRiyaa is a fine artist known for statement paintings and custom portraits, trained at European art institutes. Her work has been exhibited in Paris, Berlin, Florence, London, Delhi and Mumbai, and she counts global HNIs, CEOs, VPs and politicians among her clients. She won a Bronze medal at the All India Mandala contest. As Founder of Riyaa dartstudio and Color Caastle Art Academy, she teaches that fundamentals set creativity free. She is the author of The Portrait Atelier, a three-part series on drawing the human figure, with books on acrylics, watercolour and colour theory on the way. Her belief is simple: anyone can learn art, one fundamental at a time.Krishna RavalKrishna Raval began as an engineer and Bharatanatyam dancer, then built a career in a multinational manufacturing company while earning an MBA in Operations. A lifelong quest to understand herself led to a new path as an author and certified life coach. Krishna's book, 'Feelings, Freakouts, Figuring It Out: A Teen's Playbook to Ditching the Script', speaks to young adults trying to work out where life is headed. Also a contributor to the ICA anthology, she helps people change limiting beliefs and build lives that truly resonate with them. A lifelong learner, she explores everything from languages and spirituality to the ever-evolving world of AI. She believes everyone has a story worth telling and deserves a space where they feel safe, heard, and accepted without judgment.Dr. Kunti NagwekarDr. Kunti Nagwekar is an educationist and corporate trainer who has taught Eye Yoga since 1996. After 27 years as a lecturer in Mumbai, she founded Sampoorna Wellbeing Technology and earned a PhD in "Mind and Vision." Her Creative Visualisation courses have reached corporates, business owners, the Armed Forces and film personalities. A full-time Sevak with MaitriBodh Parivaar, she wrote My Divine Talks To Me! in 36 days. It won recognition from the International Council of Authors and sold 160 copies in eight days, by word of mouth. Its message is simple: the Divine lives in your heart, as your closest friend. Her next book is Eye Care for You.Padmaa Priyaa K.RPadmaa Priyaa K.R is the founder of Gaaya The Mother, a Tarot reader and coach, space and energy healer, tarot artist and author. Her work weaves together Tarot, space alchemy, numerology, art and writing, helping women who have spent years putting themselves last reconnect with their voice. A teacher at heart, she specialises in reading Tarot through symbols and even shows students how to hand-make their own decks. She is the author of The Humans We Forgot to Become and created Tattva Tarot: The Path to Your Soul, a 108-card deck and companion book rooted in Sanskrit words and Indian culture. Her vision: a community where women learn, create and lead.Adv. Juhi DamodarAdv. Juhi Damodar is a legal professional practising since 1998, beginning at the Mumbai High Court, Maharashtra and Goa Bench, and now Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee, Udupi. A TEDx Speaker and recipient of the Global Women in Business and Leadership Award 2025, she wrote Justice for Every Child, a practical guide to the POCSO Act, 2012 that blends law, psychology and rehabilitation, covered by ANI, The Tribune and others. Known for her work on child rights and third-party parental alienation, she also speaks on public health and law at the ECIPH Dialogue. Her aim: law that keeps pace with lived realities and gives every child a stronger voice.Together, these ten journeys show that leadership today is not defined by a single industry, title or path. It is defined by the willingness to keep learning, to create with courage and to serve with purpose. As the world continues to change, the people featured here are a reminder that the future belongs to those who turn insight into action and ideas into impact, and who, in doing so, open the door for others to follow.The pages slugged ‘Brand Connect’ are equivalent to advertisements and are not written and produced by Forbes India journalists.

stories.headline: Sebi bars Avadhut Sathe, academy from markets, imposes ₹11.5 crore penalty
stories.title: Sebi bars Avadhut Sathe, academy from markets, imposes ₹11.5 crore penalty
stories.summary: In a final order issued on Friday, the market regulator directed ASTAPL and its founder Avadhut Dinkar Sathe to disgorge and refund ₹546.17 crore to eligible investors and participants who paid for its unregistered services.
reasons: source: event has 4 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'sebi bars' in title weight 42
event term: 'market regulator' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has imposed penalties totalling ₹11.5 crore on Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy Pvt.
Ltd (ASTAPL) and its directors, and barred them from accessing the securities markets for periods of up to two years for providing unregistered investment advisory and research analyst activities.

In a final order issued on Friday, the market regulator directed ASTAPL and its founder Avadhut Dinkar Sathe to disgorge and refund ₹546.17 crore to eligible investors and participants who paid for its unregistered services.
It has also ordered a deposit of ₹67.87 crore in interest with Sebi’s Investor Protection and Education Fund.
Sebi imposed a penalty of ₹6 crore on ASTAPL, ₹4 crore on Sathe and ₹1.5 crore on Gouri Avadhut Sathe, another director.

stories.headline: Tata Motors CV turns in profit of Rs1,254 crore; revenue surges 42 percent
stories.title: Tata Motors CV turns in profit of Rs1,254 crore; revenue surges 42 percent
stories.summary: Tata Motors, the commercial vehicle business of the Tata Group, clocked consolidated net profit of Rs1,254 crore in the September quarter (Q2 of FY27) compared with a loss of Rs867 crore a year earlier.The company plunged into the red last year because of a Rs2,027 crore mark-to-market loss on Tata Capital investment.In Q2 this fiscal, revenue rose 36 percent to Rs25,338 crore, while Ebitda (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) increased 31 percent to about Rs2,800 crore.“This is the highest ever revenue in any second quarter yet,” Girish Wagh, MD & CEO of Tata Motors, said on a post-results media call.The Q2 performance was supported by a 42 percent increase in wholesale volumes to 1,35,100 vehicles, with domestic and export volumes rising 30 percent and 177 percent, respectively.Also Read: Stellantis and Tata Motors to develop cars for 50 global marketsThe management said sustained infrastructure activity and stable fleet utilisation continue to support demand.Profit before exceptional items and tax stood at Rs1,780 crore, compared with a loss of Rs551 crore a year earlier.Its standalone revenue rose 42 percent to Rs23,930 crore, while net profit was Rs2,138 crore, compared with a loss of Rs1,021 crore in the year-earlier quarter.Margins under pressureConsolidated Ebitda margin was 10.9 percent, down 40 basis points from a year earlier, while standalone Ebitda margin was 11.7 percent, lower by 90 basis points. Ebitda rose 31 percent on both the standalone and consolidated measures, slower than revenue growth.The company said commodity cost pressures persisted through the first half of the financial year, particularly for steel and rubber.“We’re expecting further commodity increase in Q3, in metals, tires and rubber,” said Wagh.The company said it has taken a three-pronged approach to managing cost inflation.“The first line of attack is to keep driving cost efficiencies (variable costs). The second one is to control the expenses (fixed costs). And the third is to take calibrated price increases,” according to the MD.The CV maker has taken three price hikes this fiscal: Up to 1.5 percent from April 1, up to 2.5 percent from July 1 and up to 1 percent from October 1.Wagh said the company will take a call towards the end of Q3 on the price hike action for Q4.The company’s domestic market share in retail stood at 36.2 percent for the first half of FY27, an increase of 110 basis points from FY26.Its market share was 55.7 percent in heavy commercial vehicles, 36.3 percent in intermediate and light commercial vehicles, 27.6 percent in small commercial vehicles and pickups, and 41.1 percent in commercial passenger vehicles.Tata Motors expects the CV market to remain supported by infrastructure spending and freight activity, but it cautioned that growth rates will moderate in the second half of FY27 against a higher base.It, nonetheless, expects the industry to post double-digit growth for this fiscal year. “We hope to surpass [industry numbers] and overdeliver as we did in H1,” said Wagh.On a consolidated basis, free cash flow was Rs3,044 crore, up Rs1,007 crore from a year earlier, and the net cash position stood at Rs15,900 crore.Also Read: Festive season auto retail sales fall 6.5 percent on short Navratri, high baseIveco DealThe company’s Euro3.9 billion acquisition of European CV maker Iveco Group continues to progress well and is in line with expectations, said the management.The deal has been delayed because of opposition from some minority shareholders.The current acceptance level for the deal stands at 35 percent even as the tender offer ends on October 26.“As is typically seen in tender offer processes, a significant proportion of shares tend to be tendered towards the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours,” said Wagh.The company this month raised its offer to Euro14.4 per share from the earlier Euro14.1.“This is our best and final offer,” said Wagh. “We increased our offer in view of the delay in the overall process as compared to the initial timeline that we had indicated. There was a delay of around four months. Therefore, we have come up with this Euro14.4 [offer], which is a goodwill gesture from our side.”At the Extraordinary General Meeting held on October 16, Iveco shareholders approved all the resolutions proposed by the Board of Directors.One of those was reducing the minimum acceptance level of the Tata offer to 80 percent, from 95 percent earlier, of the common shares.“Looking at the EGM result and the support that we have got, we are quite confident that we should be able to cross the threshold of 80 percent,” said Wagh.Subject to successful completion of the tender offer, settlement is scheduled for October 30. “Consolidation of Iveco will begin next quarter and our priority will be on delivering seamless transition,” according to the management.

opening: Tata Motors, the commercial vehicle business of the Tata Group, clocked consolidated net profit of Rs1,254 crore in the September quarter (Q2 of FY27) compared with a loss of Rs867 crore a year earlier.
The company plunged into the red last year because of a Rs2,027 crore mark-to-market loss on Tata Capital investment.
body: In Q2 this fiscal, revenue rose 36 percent to Rs25,338 crore, while Ebitda (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) increased 31 percent to about Rs2,800 crore.
“This is the highest ever revenue in any second quarter yet,” Girish Wagh, MD & CEO of Tata Motors, said on a post-results media call.
The Q2 performance was supported by a 42 percent increase in wholesale volumes to 1,35,100 vehicles, with domestic and export volumes rising 30 percent and 177 percent, respectively.
The management said sustained infrastructure activity and stable fleet utilisation continue to support demand.
Profit before exceptional items and tax stood at Rs1,780 crore, compared with a loss of Rs551 crore a year earlier.
Ebitda rose 31 percent on both the standalone and consolidated measures, slower than revenue growth.
The company said commodity cost pressures persisted through the first half of the financial year, particularly for steel and rubber.
“We’re expecting further commodity increase in Q3, in metals, tires and rubber,” said Wagh.
The company said it has taken a three-pronged approach to managing cost inflation.
“The first line of attack is to keep driving cost efficiencies (variable costs).
The second one is to control the expenses (fixed costs).
And the third is to take calibrated price increases,” according to the MD.
Wagh said the company will take a call towards the end of Q3 on the price hike action for Q4.

Tata Motors expects the CV market to remain supported by infrastructure spending and freight activity, but it cautioned that growth rates will moderate in the second half of FY27 against a higher base.
It, nonetheless, expects the industry to post double-digit growth for this fiscal year.
“We hope to surpass [industry numbers] and overdeliver as we did in H1,” said Wagh.
On a consolidated basis, free cash flow was Rs3,044 crore, up Rs1,007 crore from a year earlier, and the net cash position stood at Rs15,900 crore.
Iveco Deal.
The deal has been delayed because of opposition from some minority shareholders.
The current acceptance level for the deal stands at 35 percent even as the tender offer ends on October 26.

“As is typically seen in tender offer processes, a significant proportion of shares tend to be tendered towards the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours,” said Wagh.
The company this month raised its offer to Euro14.4 per share from the earlier Euro14.1.
“This is our best and final offer,” said Wagh.
“We increased our offer in view of the delay in the overall process as compared to the initial timeline that we had indicated.
There was a delay of around four months.

Therefore, we have come up with this Euro14.4 [offer], which is a goodwill gesture from our side.” At the Extraordinary General Meeting held on October 16, Iveco shareholders approved all the resolutions proposed by the Board of Directors.
“Looking at the EGM result and the support that we have got, we are quite confident that we should be able to cross the threshold of 80 percent,” said Wagh.
Subject to successful completion of the tender offer, settlement is scheduled for October 30.
“Consolidation of Iveco will begin next quarter and our priority will be on delivering seamless transition,” according to the management.

stories.headline: India’s bulk Scotch tariff dispute risks undermining India-UK trade deal, industry group says
stories.title: India’s bulk Scotch tariff dispute risks undermining India-UK trade deal, industry group says
stories.summary: An industry association has sought urgent clarification from the government as the tariff dispute raises concerns over market access and investment
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters.

Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of protracted negotiations leading up to the deal's July 15 implementation, though India ultimately agreed to halve import taxes on certain Scotch imports from 150% to 75% immediately and to 40% over 10 years.
The British government said "iconic UK products" like whiskies would benefit from the pact.

Indian investigators, however, have privately told companies the reduced rate does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, creating the first significant dispute over the free trade agreement since it took effect.

India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence searched the offices of Pernod and Diageo and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products to benefit from the reduced rate.

In a letter to the commerce minister on Friday, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India (ISWAI) wrote that the classification issue "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom."
"The preferential tariff treatment negotiated...
could effectively become unavailable for these imports," continued the letter, a copy of which was seen by Reuters.
ISWAI declined to comment on its letter, while India's commerce ministry did not immediately respond.
Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, declined to comment, and Diageo did not respond to a request for comment.
Both told Reuters earlier this week that they were cooperating with Indian authorities carrying out the investigation.
Import tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, who have in the past faced demands for large amounts of back-tax.

stories.headline: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.title: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.summary: 358 mandals provisionally identified as drought-affected based on rainfall, crop coverage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought and El Nino conditions chaired by Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka on Friday resolved to prepare a comprehensive and department-wise action plan to tackle the drought caused by El Nino conditions.

The plans will focus on safeguarding supply of water for drinking and irrigation and ensuring uninterrupted electricity, agricultural support and rural employment so that people do not face hardships in the coming days.

The first meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee, constituted to review the drought and El Nino situation in the State and recommend appropriate measures to the government, was held here on Friday (October 23).
The meeting primarily discussed the impact of El Nino and drought in various parts of the State, water availability, relief measures for farmers and future action plans.

Sub-Committee members and Ministers N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, D. Seethakka, Tummala Nageswara Rao and Vakiti Srihari along with Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and secretaries of the concerned departments attended the meeting.
Mr. Vikramarka asked the officials to scientifically assess drought conditions and examine the mandals eligible for declaration as drought-affected areas under the prescribed guidelines.
He stressed that the government’s priority was to minimise the impact of drought and ensure timely delivery of necessary assistance to people through coordinated efforts.
He instructed officials to assess not only areas already experiencing severe drought but also mandals where the drought impact exceeds 20%.
An advance assessment of the likely impact of drought on various sectors would help the government provide timely assistance to those in need, he said.
He suggested that every department identify the challenges and prepare a clear action plan to address them.
He asked the officials to anticipate challenges in the power sector arising from El Nino conditions and take measures in advance.
Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy asked the District Collectors to conduct weekly review meetings with the officials concerned to monitor the measures being implemented to address the drought conditions.

stories.headline: Govt announces 25 crore development projects for Beerwah
stories.title: Govt announces 25 crore development projects for Beerwah
stories.summary: Budgam, Oct 23: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday said his government was making every effort to accelerate development across the Union Territory, asserting that his visit to Beerwah was aimed at reviewing and advancing key development projects in the constituency. Speaking to reporters at Beerwah tehsil, the Chief Minister said several development initiatives had been taken up in the area, with a focus on improving infrastructure, road connectivity, electricity supply and public amenities. Recalling his association with the Beerwah Assembly constituency, Omar Abdullah said he had been elected as its MLA in the 2014 Assembly elections and had remained committed to fulfilling the promises made to the people. “I have a long-standing relationship with Beerwah. When the people elected me as their representative in 2014, I promised to work for the development of the constituency. After the formation of our government, we initiated several development projects here,” he said. The Chief Minister said around ₹25 crore had been allocated for various development works in Beerwah. Of the six projects, one has been inaugurated, while foundation stones have been laid for the remaining five. He said each project was important for addressing the developmental needs of the constituency. Highlighting the completion of a long-pending public demand, Omar Abdullah said a bridge over Nallah Sukhnag, which had been damaged in the 2014 floods, had been reconstructed and handed over to the public. “The bridge was a long-pending demand of the people. I am thankful to the Deputy Chief Minister and the concerned department for completing the work within a short period. The bridge has now been handed over to the people,” he said. The Chief Minister said measures were also being taken to improve the appearance of Beerwah town. The foundation stone has been laid for a walking track and decks along the banks of Nallah Sukhnag. In addition, ₹4 crore has been earmarked for the construction and improvement of lanes and drains in the Beerwah main town. On electricity infrastructure, Omar Abdullah said the capacity of the receiving station in Beerwah would be enhanced to improve power supply to the area. He said the work was expected to be completed within five months. He added that the foundation stone had also been laid for a transformer workshop at the Beerwah receiving station, where damaged transformers could be repaired, helping improve the maintenance of the local power distribution network. Addressing concerns over road development, the Chief Minister said several road projects had been delayed due to the India-Pakistan conflict and a shortage of raw materials. He said funds had already been provided for road development and macadamisation, adding that roads approved during the current year were expected to be completed next year. Omar Abdullah also assured residents that pending development works would receive attention. Responding to the demand for a stadium in Beerwah, he said a suitable site would be identified to enable the Sports Department to take up the project. The Chief Minister also addressed concerns over the proposed diversion of traffic from the national highway passing through the centre of Beerwah town. Residents have expressed apprehensions that diverting traffic could affect local businesses and commercial activity. He said the matter had been taken up with the concerned highway authorities and that efforts would be made to address the concerns of the local population. When asked about a possible Cabinet expansion and other political issues, Omar Abdullah declined to comment, saying his focus during the visit was on development projects and road-related concerns in Beerwah.
